lessons.title: Cash Management Overview and Work Areas
Banks, Bank Branches and Bank Accounts

slots.practicalActivity: Using Harborview Metals Inc. (the course's own worked example) as your scenario, build a three-level Bank -> Branch -> Account diagram showing one bank with at least two branches and a bank account at each branch, labeling which work area (Cash Management and Banking, Cash Positioning, or Cash Forecasting) you'd use to set each one up. Then write 2-3 sentences explaining, in your own words, what Cash Management explicitly does NOT do (it doesn't initiate payments or record what customers owe) and which modules actually own those actions.
slots.deliverable: A labeled Bank -> Branch -> Account hierarchy diagram for Harborview Metals Inc., plus a short written explanation of what Cash Management does not own.

slots.practicalActivity: Design a bank-account-access policy for Harborview Metals Inc.: list at least 4 distinct roles (for example an AP disbursement clerk, a Treasury analyst, an AR cash-application clerk, and an external auditor) and specify, for each, whether it needs Payment, Receipt, Bank Statement, or full Cash Management Administration access on a given bank account. Then write a short go-live checklist of what you'd confirm is in place before turning on automatic reconciliation for a brand-new account.
slots.deliverable: A 4-role bank-account-access matrix for Harborview Metals Inc., plus a written pre-go-live reconciliation-setup checklist.

lessons.title: Bank Statement Formats: BAI2, MT940 and CAMT.053

slots.practicalActivity: Harborview Metals Inc. has a US operating account that receives BAI2 files and a UK subsidiary account that receives CAMT.053 files. Write out, side by side, how each format marks an opening balance, one transaction line, and a closing balance (referencing BAI2's `03`/`16`/`49` record codes and MT940/CAMT's tagged-field equivalents), then write the loading/import steps you'd follow in Oracle to get each file into the same internal statement structure despite their different source formats.
slots.deliverable: A side-by-side BAI2-vs-CAMT.053 structure comparison for Harborview's two accounts, plus a written statement-import walkthrough for each format.

slots.practicalActivity: List 5 realistic bank statement transaction codes Harborview Metals Inc. might see on its BAI2 file (for example a wire transfer in, a lockbox deposit, a service charge, an NSF return, interest earned) and map each one to the kind of system transaction it should eventually reconcile against. Then write a 3-step troubleshooting script for a statement line that failed to load because of a formatting error, naming exactly what you'd check first, second, and third before re-attempting the import.
slots.deliverable: A 5-code transaction-mapping table plus a 3-step statement-import-error troubleshooting script.

slots.practicalActivity: Recreate Harborview Metals Inc.'s two matching rules from the lesson in a table: a one-to-one rule for its operating account (source: Receivables Receipts; criteria: amount and value date; a $0.02 tolerance) and a one-to-many rule for its lockbox account (one statement line matched against several individual receipts). For each rule, write out transaction source, match type, grouping, and criteria. Then explain why that same $0.02 tolerance rule would be rejected if someone tried to attach it to the one-to-many lockbox rule instead.
slots.deliverable: A two-rule matching-rule specification table (operating account + lockbox account) plus a written explanation of the one-to-one-only tolerance restriction.

lessons.title: Reconciling Payables Payments and Receivables Receipts

slots.practicalActivity: Work through a scenario where 3 of Harborview's statement lines failed to auto-match: a duplicate wire, a receipt posted against the wrong account, and a bank fee with no corresponding system transaction yet. For each, decide and justify whether you'd manually match it, create a new system transaction for it, or leave it unreconciled pending research. Then write out, specifically, how a Payables payment and a Receivables receipt each travel from their own subledger into Cash Management's reconciliation queue.
slots.deliverable: A 3-item manual-reconciliation decision log with justifications, plus a written explanation of how Payables payments and Receivables receipts reach the reconciliation queue.

slots.practicalActivity: Harborview's month-end review turns up 6 unreconciled items sitting for over 30 days. Categorize each into a plausible root cause (timing difference, data entry error, missing transaction, bank error) and write an aging-based escalation plan for items past 30/60/90 days. Then name which reconciliation report you'd pull to prove to an external auditor that the operating account is fully reconciled as of month-end, and what it would need to show.
slots.deliverable: A 6-item unreconciled-item aging log with an escalation plan, plus a named audit-ready reconciliation report and what it must show.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending practice for Reconciliation: write a single end-to-end scenario where Harborview Metals Inc. loads a new bank statement, runs automatic reconciliation against a rule set you define (naming the match type and any tolerance), manually clears two exceptions you invent, and then pulls the correct report to confirm the account is fully reconciled -- tying together matching rules, automatic and manual reconciliation, and reporting from the whole chapter.
slots.deliverable: One written end-to-end reconciliation walkthrough (load -> auto-match -> manual exception handling -> report) combining every lesson in the Reconciliation chapter.

slots.practicalActivity: Harborview's operating account shows a $24 monthly bank fee and $140 of interest earned directly on this month's statement -- neither originated in Payables or Receivables. Record both as external cash transactions (one outflow, one inflow) with the correct transaction type. Then design a same-day bank account transfer moving $50,000 from the operating account into a short-term investment account, specifying the source account, destination account, and amount you'd enter.
slots.deliverable: Two recorded external cash transactions (the fee and the interest) plus one bank-account-transfer specification with source, destination, and amount.

slots.practicalActivity: Reproduce Harborview Metals Inc.'s Monday cash position by hand: starting from a $220,000 opening balance with $340,000 in expected inflows and $410,000 in expected outflows, calculate the projected end-of-week balance and state whether it clears the $100,000 minimum balance target. Then sketch a 13-week forecast template with rows for open Payables invoices, open Receivables invoices, and a trend-based 'miscellaneous cash sales' category in weekly columns, labeling each row transaction-based or trend-based.
slots.deliverable: A worked Monday cash-position calculation against the $100,000 minimum, plus a 13-week forecast template with each row labeled transaction-based or trend-based.

slots.practicalActivity: Write out the journal-entry flow for the $24 bank fee you recorded two slots ago, naming the debit and credit accounts you'd expect Create Accounting to generate for an external cash transaction. Then, using this course's own troubleshooting-practice lesson as your model, pick 3 realistic Cash Management problems (a statement that won't import, a rule that won't auto-match, a position that looks wrong) and write a root-cause-and-fix script for each, the way you would walk a junior consultant through them.
slots.deliverable: One worked journal-entry flow for the bank-fee transaction, plus a 3-problem Cash Management troubleshooting script.

slots.practicalActivity: Course capstone lab: build one continuous Harborview Metals Inc. scenario end to end in writing -- set up a bank, branch, and account; define a reconciliation rule set with at least one tolerance; load and reconcile a statement with 2 exceptions you invent and resolve; record one external cash transaction; and close with a cash-position statement showing whether the account clears its minimum balance. This should read as a single coherent treasury workflow, not disconnected answers to separate questions.
slots.deliverable: One continuous written Cash Management capstone walkthrough covering account setup, reconciliation, external transactions, and cash positioning for Harborview Metals Inc.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After this course, a student can set up and secure the bank account hierarchy, load and reconcile bank statements (automatically and manually) against Payables payments and Receivables receipts, handle unreconciled exceptions, and build a short-term cash position and longer-range forecast in Oracle Fusion Cash Management.
